newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Soldiers loot house of Mobutu's ex-premier.
newsitem.headline: Soldiers loot house of Mobutu's ex-premier.

text.p: Armed men believed to be victorious Alliance rebels looted the house of Zaire's exiled former prime minister Kengo wa Dondo on Tuesday, family employees said on Thursday.
"About 10 soldiers came twice on Tuesday and were helped by local people," Pascal Ntambue told Reuters at the luxury residence in Kinshasa's Binza suburb.
"But the Alliance came and arrested some of them," he said.
The looters made off with five television sets, eight music systems, computers, video cassette players and 50 pairs of shoes, one servant said during a tour of the house.

Precious ornaments, crystal, furniture and a valuable stamp collection were untouched. So were framed and signed photographs of Kengo with dignitaries such as U.S. Vice President Dan Quayle and French Prime Minister Alain Juppe.
"The Alliance soldiers who arrested the looters requisitioned two jeeps - one Mercedes and one Pajero - but they got us to sign an official paper," he said.
The employees said the uniformed looters were apparently from Laurent Kabila's victorious Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL).

The soldiers did not speak Lingala, the main language in western Zaire. They spoke English and Swahili, indicating they were foreigners from East Africa. Many of Kabila's fighters, who captured Kinshasa on May 17, are from Burundi, Rwanda and Uganda, diplomats and Kinshasa residents say.

Mobutu's defeated soldiers looted widely for 48 hours after their defeat on Saturday. Alliance troops have built a solid reputation for discipline during their seven-month campaign but the temptations in Kinshasa seem to have been overwhelming for some.
Witnesses report that severe punishment is meted out by the Alliance to miscreants in its ranks.
Kengo was a pillar of the Mobutu administration for most of its 32 years. He left the country in April after he was removed as prime minister by Zaire's former transitional parliament.
Members of his household said Kengo and his wife were currently in Belgium after staying at their house in Marbella, Spain.
